outcome.answer:
LLM agents can reuse specific workflows by turning past trajectories into reusable skills or procedural units, then recalling those skills for similar new tasks instead of rerunning the full workflow. LifeMem clusters interaction trajectories by underlying workflows and recalls relevant skills and trajectories at inference time to guide actions, which reduces forgetting and improves transfer [1]. TRIAGE similarly abstracts historical trajectories into reusable skills for identical or similar queries, including deterministic parameter substitution for close matches [10].

Other papers use related ideas at different levels: SWIFT transfers structural priors and workflow demonstrations to synthesize a complete workflow in one pass [2], while MENTOR synthesizes a history-dependent runtime shield from a procedural manual so repeated workflows can be handled consistently [6]. For avoiding forgetting specifically, LifeMem reports reduced forgetting, and the study on continual learning in memory notes that abstract procedural memories transfer more reliably than detailed trajectories, but memory design can still induce forgetting [1, 3].
